newsitem.title: USA: Sabre Group soars in initial public offering.
newsitem.headline: Sabre Group soars in initial public offering.

text.p: The stock of Sabre Group Holdings Inc., AMR Corp.'s airline reservations and information system, soared Friday in very heavy volume after more than 20 million shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The initial public offering by AMR, the parent of American Airlines, of 20.2 million shares of Sabre, or about 16 percent of the company, was priced at $27 a share, but enthusiastic investors pushed it up to $32.75 by early afternoon, with almost 8 million shares changing hands.

The IPO raised about $662 million for Sabre, which intends to expand further into the information services business, where it faces stiff competition from computer systems companies such as Electronic Data Systems Corp. and Computer Sciences Corp.

The company the Sabre system, a real-time transaction processing system that operates from an underground computer facility in Tulsa, Okla., and which can be accessed by more than 120,000 computer terminals around the world.
More than half of Sabre's $1.5 billion in 1995 revenues came from air travel and other reservation bookings made by travel agents, with the balance coming from its information systems services.
AMR stock added $1 to $86.375 in afternoon trading, also on the NYSE.
